groups.defect: Destinations without credentialId are routed to Google's primary calendar instead of their configured calendar, and the fallback creation branch omits externalId from the stored booking reference.
groups.rationale: All four report both the credential-only destination lookup and the omitted externalId argument. The merged comment must retain the provider routing fix and the reference metadata fix.

groups.defect: Google updateEvent and deleteEvent search for a destination matching an already-falsy externalCalendarId, losing the configured-calendar fallback in both operations.
groups.rationale: The same erroneous fallback appears in update and delete, and several suggestions explicitly report both occurrences. Both expressions need correction; references lacking calendar IDs are the triggering context.

groups.defect: A null destinationCalendar makes the optional-chained push silently discard collective hosts' destination calendars.
groups.rationale: Both describe the same initialization and append failure when the organizer and event type have no destination calendar. Initializing or assigning the array correctly resolves both.

groups.defect: The Google Meet fallback dereferences an undefined first destination calendar when destinationCalendar is null or empty.
groups.rationale: Every suggestion reports the missing null guard on mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration. One optional-chaining correction addresses all five.

groups.defect: Credential database fallbacks in creation, update, and cancellation use stored credential IDs without checking ownership or rejecting invalid credentials.
groups.rationale: These report the same unchecked credential lookup repeated across three execution paths. Each lookup needs the ownership and validity checks preserved in the merged comment.

groups.defect: Office365, Lark, and BaseCalendarService select the first destination instead of the destination belonging to the active credential, causing incorrect calendar targeting and inconsistent references.
groups.rationale: All three identify the same first-destination assumption across the same provider implementations. Correcting the selection requires edits in each affected implementation.
